V1.1.note: Input is decoded once at the API boundary by FastAPI and Pydantic; output is encoded by React and by template autoescaping.

V1.2.note: ORM with bound parameters; no string-built queries.

V1.3.note: Sanitization of data passed to dangerous contexts.

V1.4.note: Application code is Python and TypeScript, which manage memory. Native parsers (PDFium, OpenCV, ZBar) are kept patched (V15) and run in the sandboxed worker (threat T26).

V1.5.note: No unsafe deserialization: Celery uses JSON only (D60), models load from safetensors only (T42).

V2.1.note: Validation rules, consistency rules and business limits are documented in REQUIREMENTS.md sections 4.1 to 4.3.

V2.2.note: Server-side validation with Pydantic models against the rules in REQUIREMENTS.md 4.1.

V2.3.note: Business logic flows (approvals, issue, archive) enforced server-side.

V2.4.note: Rate limits and queue limits from REQUIREMENTS.md 4.3.

V3.2.note: React renders text safely; downloads use Content-Disposition attachment and nosniff.

V3.3.note: Session cookie uses the __Host- prefix, Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict.

V3.4.note: Security headers set by nginx and the API.

V3.5.note: CSRF token plus Origin check on state-changing requests.

V3.7.note: Modern supported browser technology only; no redirects to other domains.

V4.1.note: Correct Content-Type with charset; HTTPS redirect only for browser pages; proxy headers set by nginx only.

V4.2.note: nginx and Uvicorn configured to reject ambiguous message framing.

V4.4.note: No WebSocket. Job status is polled over HTTPS.

V5.1.note: Permitted types, extensions, sizes and safety handling documented in REQUIREMENTS.md 4.4.

V5.2.note: Size limits and magic-byte type checks at upload.

V5.3.note: Files stored under server-generated names in object storage, never in a web-served folder.

V5.4.note: Downloads served with a server-chosen, encoded file name.

V6.1.note: Brute-force defences, context-specific words and the single authentication pathway documented in REQUIREMENTS.md 4.5.

V6.3.note: Password plus TOTP for all staff.

V6.4.note: Random initial passwords; no hints; reset and lost-TOTP recovery need a Supervisor's second approval and TOTP re-enrolment.

V6.5.note: TOTP with single use, defined lifetime, CSPRNG seeds; backup codes hashed with Argon2id.

V6.6.note: No out-of-band (SMS, e-mail or push) authentication. TOTP only.

V7.1.note: Timeouts and concurrent session limit documented in REQUIREMENTS.md 4.6.

V7.2.note: Server-side reference session tokens from a CSPRNG, at least 128 bits, renewed at login.

V7.4.note: Logout ends the server session; disabled users lose all sessions.

V7.5.note: Re-authentication for sensitive account changes; users can view and end their sessions.

V8.1.note: Function, data and field level rules in ACCESS_MATRIX.md (Phase 17). The role summary is already in REQUIREMENTS.md section 1.

V8.2.note: Role and case membership checked in one dependency on every route.

V8.3.note: All authorization enforced in the API, never in the UI.

V9.1.note: Sessions do not use self-contained tokens. The QR-sealed copy payload is a self-contained signed token: Ed25519 only, verified with a pinned key.

V9.2.note: The QR payload carries a fixed type and is accepted only by the verify service.

V11.1.note: Key management policy (designed in line with NIST SP 800-57) and cryptographic inventory in KEY_MANAGEMENT.md.

V11.2.note: pyca cryptography only; algorithm identifiers stored with every record for crypto agility.

V11.4.note: SHA-256 and HMAC-SHA-256 only; no MD5 or SHA1 for any security purpose (D66).

V11.5.note: Python secrets module (CSPRNG) for all tokens and codes.

V12.1.note: TLS 1.2 and 1.3 only, strong cipher suites, at nginx.

V12.3.note: TLS on internal connections to PostgreSQL, SeaweedFS and OpenBao with an internal CA.

V13.1.note: All communication needs documented in REQUIREMENTS.md 4.7.

V13.2.note: Per-service credentials, least privilege, egress allowlist.

V13.3.note: Secrets in OpenBao with least-privilege policies.

V13.4.note: No debug mode, directory listing, TRACE or unintended docs in the demo deployment.

V14.1.note: Data classes and protection rules documented in REQUIREMENTS.md 4.8.

V14.2.note: Protection of sensitive data per REQUIREMENTS.md 4.8.

V14.3.note: No sensitive data kept in the browser beyond the session cookie; cleared at logout.

V15.2.note: CI audits enforce the remediation time frames.

V16.2.note: Structured logs with who, what, when and where.

V16.4.note: Logs protected by the Merkle transparency log.

V17.1.note: The system does not use WebRTC.

V17.2.note: The system does not use WebRTC.

V17.3.note: The system does not use WebRTC.

V1.2.2.note: URLs built from server IDs only; only https links allowed.

V1.2.3.note: JSON produced by the framework serializer only.

V1.2.5.note: OCR and scanning are called as libraries or over sockets; no shell commands with user input.

V1.2.6.note: The system does not use LDAP.

V1.2.7.note: The system does not use XPath.

V1.2.8.note: The system does not use LaTeX.

V1.2.9.note: Custody search escapes user text before any regular expression use.

V1.3.2.note: No eval or dynamic code execution in the codebase; Bandit and Semgrep run on every CI run (both clean on 2026-10-16).

V1.3.4.note: SVG is not an accepted upload type (REQUIREMENTS.md 4.4).

V1.3.5.note: No user-supplied Markdown, CSS, XSL or template content.

V1.3.6.note: The server only connects to the configured TSA and tree head export target; it never fetches a user-supplied URL (REQUIREMENTS.md 4.7).

V1.3.7.note: Report templates are fixed files; data is passed as variables only.

V1.3.10.note: No user-controlled format strings; logging uses parameters.

V1.5.1.note: No XML parser reads user input. Uploads are parsed only by pdfium and Pillow, for type and page checks.

V2.2.3.note: Combined-data rules from REQUIREMENTS.md 4.2 enforced server-side.

V2.3.3.note: Document, version, stored object and custody event commit in one database transaction or not at all. A locked object written before a failed transaction cannot be removed, so it is recorded as storage.orphaned (D83).

V2.3.4.note: Each two-person approval can be used once only.

V3.5.3.note: Every state-changing action (create case, add member, upload, add version) is POST; GET routes change no evidence.

V3.5.4.note: The public verify page is served from its own hostname, separate from the staff application.

V5.2.3.note: Archives are not accepted; PDF decompressed size is capped at 200 MB.

V5.4.3.note: ClamAV scan with quarantine before intake.

V6.3.2.note: No default accounts; seeded demo accounts get random passwords shown once at setup.

V7.4.2.note: Disabling a user ends all their sessions.

V9.2.1.note: The QR payload has no validity time span: a QR-sealed copy stays verifiable, and revocation is checked against the record status at verify time.

V9.2.4.note: A separate signing key per purpose (intake seals, fingerprint records, QR payloads, tree heads, reports).

V11.4.2.note: Argon2id with parameters from current guidance.

V11.4.4.note: No keys are derived from passwords.

V12.2.2.note: The demo runs on a local network with a self-signed certificate. A publicly trusted certificate is required for any real deployment; this is documented in Phase 22.

V13.2.2.note: Separate database roles (owner for migrations, app role without DDL) and an S3 app identity without Admin rights.

V13.2.3.note: No default credentials: every password and token is generated at setup, and the app refuses placeholders.

V13.4.1.note: .git, .env and docker/secrets are excluded from every image build.

V14.2.1.note: URLs carry only server-generated UUIDs; identity travels in headers and content in the body.

V14.2.2.note: Cache-Control: no-store on all authenticated and evidence responses.

V14.2.3.note: No third-party trackers, analytics or CDNs in the UI.

V14.3.3.note: Nothing sensitive in localStorage, sessionStorage or IndexedDB.

V15.1.1.note: Remediation time frames documented in REQUIREMENTS.md 4.9.

V15.1.3.note: Resource-heavy functions and their controls documented in REQUIREMENTS.md 4.10.

V15.2.3.note: The demo image contains no tests, sample code or development endpoints.

V15.3.1.note: Response models return only required fields; the public page returns one message only.

V15.3.2.note: Outbound clients (TSA, export) do not follow redirects.

V15.3.4.note: nginx sets the client address; the API trusts it only from nginx.

V15.3.6.note: Map and Set used for user-keyed data in the UI.

V15.3.7.note: Each parameter read from one explicit source only.

V16.2.2.note: UTC timestamps; NTP sync to NIC or NPL (CERT-In direction, REQUIREMENTS.md NFR-10).

V16.2.4.note: One JSON object per log line with UTC timestamps and request IDs.

V16.3.3.note: Security events and bypass attempts logged.

V16.3.4.note: Unexpected errors and control failures logged.

V16.4.1.note: JSON encoding escapes newlines and quotes, so user text cannot forge log lines.

V16.4.3.note: Full log shipping to a separate system is out of demo scope. Signed tree heads are exported outside the system every day, so any change to logged history is detected (threats T18, T19).

V16.5.2.note: If the TSA is down, intake continues and records are marked time-stamp pending.

V16.5.3.note: Fail closed: an error during verification gives no verdict, never Equivalent.

V1.5.2.note: Task messages and results are JSON only; pickle is not accepted. Model loading (Phase 12) will be re-checked against this item.

V15.2.1.note: pip-audit and npm audit run on every CI run and weekly; no known vulnerable component on 2026-10-16.

V16.5.1.note: Unexpected errors return a generic message with a request ID; stack traces go to the server log only.

V1.1.1.note: Form and JSON input is decoded once by FastAPI; free text is NFC-normalised before it is validated, never after.

V1.1.2.note: JSON is encoded by the framework serializer and SQL values are bound by the ORM (Phase 5); React escapes output when the UI shows document data.

V1.2.4.note: All queries go through the SQLAlchemy ORM with bound parameters; no SQL is built from strings.

V2.2.1.note: Every Phase 5 input is checked against an allow list or pattern (types, extensions, roles, user IDs, document types, text length, UUIDs). Later phases add their inputs to the same layer.

V2.2.2.note: Validation runs in the API service layer; there is no client-side validation to rely on.

V5.2.1.note: 25 MB per file, 30 pages and 40 megapixels per page image, checked before decoding; the request body is cut off at the limit even without Content-Length. The 200 MB decompressed PDF limit is Phase 22 (V5.2.3).

V5.2.2.note: Type from magic bytes, extension must match, and the file must open in pdfium or Pillow; the client Content-Type is ignored.

V5.3.1.note: Originals go only to the object store under server keys; nothing is written to a folder served over HTTP.

V5.3.2.note: Storage keys are built from server IDs and the SHA-256 only. The uploader's file name is cleaned and kept as display text, never used in a path.

V11.4.1.note: SHA-256 is the evidence hash. MD5 is computed only for the S3 Content-MD5 transport check that Object Lock uploads need, marked usedforsecurity=False, and never used to prove integrity (D66, D86).

V11.4.3.note: Integrity of originals rests on SHA-256 (256-bit output).

V15.3.3.note: Each route accepts an explicit Pydantic model or named form fields; IDs, owners, hashes and timestamps are set by the server only.

V15.3.5.note: Path IDs are parsed as UUIDs and inputs as typed Pydantic fields; comparisons use typed values.
